blocks.intro: Antes de empezar, recupera lo de la clase pasada. Une cada palabra con su significado — sin mirar atrás.

pairs.r: en lo que va del trimestre

blocks.title: <ico-book></ico-book> RUNNING A MEETING · frases clave
blocks.intro: En B1 ya no solo participas en reuniones: las diriges. Eso pide frases para abrir, estar de acuerdo, discrepar sin sonar brusco, proponer y cerrar. Cinco pasos. Toca el altavoz de cada línea y repite en voz alta.

vocab.en: to be on the same page

blocks.note: Cómo funciona: tarjetas , unir , elegir respuestas , completar , escucha y ordenar . CHECK donde lo veas.

parts.html: 1 · ABRIR Y LLEVAR EL RITMO — tú marcas los tiempos

items.en: Sofia, could you start with GreenMarket?
items.sp: Das la palabra con nombre + could you.

items.en: Let's move on to the next steps.
items.sp: Pasemos a los próximos pasos. — cambias de tema.

parts.body: Let's + verbo es la forma natural de dirigir sin dar órdenes: incluye a todos. Va sin to: Let's to start. → Let's start.

parts.html: 2 · ESTAR DE ACUERDO — corto y claro

parts.body: El error más común de un hispanohablante en reuniones: I'm agree. → I agree. Agree ya es el verbo, no lleva am. Y «tener razón» es be right: You have reason. → You're right.

parts.html: 3 · DISCREPAR CON TACTO — primero reconoces, después el «pero»

items.en: I see your point, but we might miss the deadline.
items.sp: Entiendo tu punto, pero podríamos no llegar a la fecha.
No estoy seguro de estar de acuerdo. — suave, deja la puerta abierta.

parts.body: De izquierda a derecha, cada frase es más diplomática. «You're wrong» suena a ataque: critica la idea, no a la persona. Might (podría) también suaviza: no afirmas, adviertes.

parts.html: 4 · PROPONER — ideas en forma de pregunta o sugerencia

items.en: What if we show them a demo first?
items.sp: ¿Y si primero les mostramos una demo?

items.en: I'd suggest we launch on Friday as planned.
items.sp: Sugeriría que lancemos el viernes como estaba previsto.

items.en: Could we plan it for the next phase?

parts.body: Suggest no lleva «to» ni persona directa. I suggest you to wait. → I'd suggest we wait. · I suggest to launch on Friday. → I'd suggest launching on Friday.

parts.html: 5 · INTERRUMPIR, ACLARAR Y CERRAR — sin perder el control de la reunión

items.en: Sorry to jump in, but can I add something?
So, to confirm the next steps: we launch on Friday.
items.sp: Antes de cerrar, repites los acuerdos en voz alta.

blocks.title: FLASHCARDS · reuniones
blocks.intro: Toca cada tarjeta para ver la traducción.

blocks.title: <ico-star></ico-star> MARCOS LEADS THE STANDUP
blocks.intro: Sofia confía en Marcos para dirigir el standup diario por primera vez. Pero Priya está mirando, y la agenda se complica: el cliente pide un cambio de último minuto. Marcos tiene que mantener el control… con diplomacia.

blocks.title: UNE LA FRASE CON SU FUNCIÓN
blocks.intro: Toca la frase en inglés y luego su función en una reunión.

blocks.title: ELIGE LA RESPUESTA DIPLOMÁTICA
blocks.intro: Estás en una reunión. Las tres opciones se entienden, pero solo una suena profesional y está bien dicha.

lines.html: We're behind schedule. I think we should cancel the new feature.

options: I see your point, but maybe we could delay it instead of canceling?
I'm not agree. We can't cancel it.

lines.html: Marcos, can you summarize where we are with GreenMarket?

options: Sofia already knows where we are.
Why? You were in the last meeting.
Sure. So far, we've finished the design and we're testing the payments.

lines.html: …and back in 2019 we also tried a different layout, and then we changed the colors, and…

options: Sorry to jump in, but can we focus on the next steps?
Can you finish? We don't have time.

lines.html: So, are we all agreed on the new plan?

options: Yes, I think we're all on the same page. Let's wrap up.
I'm agree. The meeting is finish.

blocks.title: SUAVIZA LA FRASE
blocks.intro: En una reunión, el tono es la mitad del mensaje. Elige la palabra que suena profesional, no brusca.

items.q: ___ we focus on the next steps?
I see your point, ___ I think we should wait.
___ if we show them a demo first?
Sorry to ___ in — can I add something?
I'd ___ we launch on Friday as planned.
So, to ___ the next steps: we launch on Friday.

blocks.title: AUDIO 1 · THE STANDUP
blocks.desc: Marcos dirige el standup. El cliente quiere una función nueva. ¿Cómo lo maneja Marcos?

questions.q: What does the client want to add?
What does Marcos suggest about the new feature?
options: Ask the client to drop it
Plan it for the next phase

questions.q: What does Sofia suggest as a compromise?
options: Show the client a demo first
Ask the client to wait a month

questions.q: When do they start the live chat?

speaking.prompt: How did Marcos disagree with Priya politely? Give the phrase he used and what he suggested.
speaking.starter: He said, 'I see your point, but (his objection)', and he suggested they (his suggestion).

transcript.html: Okay everyone, let's get started. This is a quick standup, so let's keep it short. Sofia, could you start with GreenMarket?
Sure. We've finished the design, and Marcos has just tested the payments. So we're on track for Friday.
Thanks, Sofia. Let's move on to the next steps. Priya, you wanted to add something?
Yes. The client has asked for a new feature — a live chat. I think we should add it this week.
I see your point, but if we add it now, we might miss the deadline. Could we plan it for the next phase?
Hmm. But the client really wants it.
Sorry to jump in — what if we show them a demo first, and add the chat next week?
That's a good idea. Let's do that.
Great. So, to confirm the next steps: we launch on Friday, and we start the live chat on Monday. Are we all agreed?
Agreed.
Perfect. Let's wrap up. Thanks, everyone.

blocks.title: ORDENA LA FRASE DIPLOMÁTICA
blocks.intro: Toca las palabras para formar frases educadas de reunión.

items.answer: I see your point but we might miss the deadline
Sorry to jump in but can I add something
Could we focus on the next steps
What if we show them a demo first
Let's move on to the next steps

blocks.title: AUDIO 2 · THE CLIENT SYNC
blocks.desc: Marcos llama a David. El cliente presiona por la función nueva. Marcos gestiona sus expectativas.

questions.q: What does David want by Friday?
Why doesn't Marcos want to add the chat by Friday?
options: They might rush it and cause bugs
The client has not confirmed it
The chat will be ready by Friday
The site will launch next week
The chat will be ready by Monday

questions.q: What is Marcos going to send David after the call?

speaking.prompt: How did Marcos manage David's expectations? Use I understand… and I'd suggest….
speaking.starter: He said he understood it was important, but he'd suggest they launch the main site first and (next step).

transcript.html: Hi David, thanks for joining. I wanted to update you on the project and the new live chat.
Hi Marcos. Yes, the chat is really important for us. Can you add it by Friday?
I understand it's important. The thing is, if we add it by Friday, we might rush it and cause bugs.
I see. So what do you suggest?
I'd suggest we launch the main site on Friday as planned, and add the live chat next week. That way it's stable.
Hmm. Can you guarantee the chat for next Monday?
Yes, I'm confident we can have it ready by Monday. We'll test it properly first.
Okay, that sounds reasonable. Let's do that.
Great. I'll send you a summary email with the next steps. Thanks for understanding, David.
No problem. Thanks, Marcos.

blocks.title: <ico-pen></ico-pen> THE RECAP EMAIL
blocks.intro: Después de una reunión, escribe un email corto (5–7 frases) con el resumen y los próximos pasos:
checklist: Saluda y di de qué reunión se trata (Following our meeting today…)
Usa una frase para proponer con tacto (I'd suggest…)
Lista los next steps con responsables y fechas
Cierra (Let me know if you have any questions.)
blocks.placeholder: Hi team, Following our meeting today,
blocks.example:
Hi team,
Following our meeting today, here is a quick recap. We agreed to acuerdo 1. We also agreed to acuerdo 2. I'd suggest we propuesta.
Next steps: persona will tarea by día, and persona will tarea by día.
Let me know if you have any questions.
tu nombre
blocks.hw: Escribe tu email de resumen y envíamelo por WhatsApp. Después grábate presentando los next steps en voz alta, sin leer, como si cerraras la reunión.

rubric.d: Escribiste el número de frases que pide la consigna y cubriste todos los puntos.
Usaste el lenguaje de reunión (I’d suggest… / next steps) al menos 3 veces, y bien.
Un lector lo entiende sin releer: ideas unidas con conectores, sin traducir literal del español.
